name: Minnesota Valley Electric Cooperative
old_description: Paying your bill and checking your usage is safe and secure with SmartHub, our online account management tool.
about:
Minnesota Valley Electric Cooperative (MVEC) is headquartered in Jordan, Minnesota. Founded on March 6, 1937, the cooperative was formed when three small electric organizations from Carver, Le Sueur, and Scott counties merged under President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s New Deal rural electrification program. The cooperative is owned by its member-owners and operates as a not-for-profit utility.

MVEC provides electric distribution service to more than 48,500 meters across a 968-square-mile territory spanning nine Minnesota counties: Blue Earth, Carver, Dakota, Hennepin, Le Sueur, Rice, Scott, Sibley, and Waseca. The cooperative purchases wholesale power from two generation providers and maintains its own distribution infrastructure, including regular maintenance and tree-trimming programs. Notable growth milestones include the acquisition of 3,500 members from Alliant Energy in 2015 and a service-area exchange with the City of Shakopee that added 537 new services in 2022.

The cooperative serves residential, agricultural, and commercial members throughout its rural and suburban service area. Its load-management programs, branded as Energy Wise, allow participants to reduce peak demand through controlled water heating, air conditioning, and smart thermostat cycling. MVEC also sponsors community initiatives such as the National Rural Electric Cooperative Association’s Youth Tour.

MVEC’s stated mission is to be a energy partner with the privilege to serve, guided by values of safety, innovation, accountability, and cooperation. The cooperative emphasizes member ownership and local governance as its distinguishing features.

name: Mira Plastics Co. Inc
old_description: WELCOME TO MIRA PLASTICS - ONE OF THE PREMIER INJECTION MOLDING COMPANIES
about:
Mira Plastics Co. Inc., a family-owned plastic injection molding company, was established in 1955 in Fredon Township, New Jersey (mailing address Newton, NJ). The business began producing hobby and recreational items before expanding into a full-service molder for a broad range of industries.

The company operates a 62,000-square-foot, climate-controlled facility equipped with injection molding machines ranging from 60 to 1,250 tons, all served by robotic part removal. In addition to thermoplastic molding, Mira Plastics provides in-house 3D CAD part design, injection molding simulation analysis, and 3D prototype printing. Secondary services include ultrasonic welding (up to 2,000 watts), hot stamping (up to 15 tons), heat transfer decal application, threaded insert staking, packaging, warehousing, and distribution. The firm works with both commodity- and engineering-grade thermoplastic resins, offering resin selection expertise.

Mira Plastics serves industrial, commercial, medical, cosmetic, electronic, domestic, and food-and-beverage markets across the United States. Its customer base includes businesses in all 50 states, with the company emphasizing its ability to support projects from prototype through high-volume production.

The company highlights its solar-powered, ISO-certified facility and its family-owned heritage as key differentiators. It also stresses expertise in complex mold configurations—including two-plate, three-plate, runner-less, and hydraulic core-pull molds—and a deep knowledge of polymer rheology to optimize material selection for each project.

about:
Mirac, LLC, operating as Mirac Tabtronics, was founded in 2001 and is headquartered in Lynchburg, Ohio, with additional facilities in Dayton and Manchester. The company operates as a contract manufacturer providing electronics manufacturing and turnkey solutions. Ownership details and founders are not publicly disclosed.

The company specializes in printed circuit board assembly, wire processing, and full box-build/turnkey assembly. Its engineering team covers electrical, software, and manufacturing disciplines under one roof, supporting concept development through production transition. Equipment includes 15 presses, five cut-and-strip wire machines, and a Schleuniger Crimp Center 36 S, enabling volumes from small to large runs. Facilities are described as state-of-the-art, staffed by a team with over 200 years of combined management and manufacturing experience.

Mirac serves customers in gaming, consumer electronics, transportation, industrial, micro-mobility, medical, military, and banking sectors. The company works with OEMs and other businesses seeking flexible, scalable manufacturing partnerships.

Mirac emphasizes on-time delivery, competitive pricing, and a quality management system focused on continual improvement. Its differentiation lies in the ability to modify facilities, equipment, and personnel to match specific production requirements, and in housing all engineering functions internally to streamline the concept-to-production handoff.

name: Miscellaneous Stainless & Steel Works LLC (MSSW LLC)
old_description: Providing fabrication and installation services for Stainless Steel, Aluminum, and Mild Steel applications.
about:
Miscellaneous Stainless & Steel Works LLC (MSSW) was founded in 2004 in Durham, North Carolina. The company is owner‑operated and specializes in custom metal fabrication and installation for commercial, industrial, and retail projects across the state.

The shop works with stainless steel, aluminum, and mild steel, offering welding (TIG and MIG), clean‑edge finishing, CAD‑driven design, and on‑site installation. Every team member is an AWS‑certified welder, and the crew handles projects from initial site measurement through final fitting, including repairs and retrofits.

MSSW serves retail and restaurant chains, industrial and utility clients, healthcare and laboratory facilities, and general contractors. Past work includes air‑handling platforms at NC State University, custom countertops for BurgerFi, architectural steel frames at Lynnhaven Mall, bumper rails for Chapel Hill Hospital, and a full kitchen fabrication for a Chapel Hill deli.

The company emphasizes durability and integrity, describing its work as “engineered, inspected, and installed with care.” It positions itself on fast turnaround, code‑compliant results, and a field‑tested, inspector‑ready approach that aims to get the job right the first time.

name: Mishimoto Automotive
old_description: For the best experience on our site, be sure to turn on Javascript in your browser.
about:
Mishimoto Automotive was founded in 2005 in Garnet Valley, Pennsylvania, by automotive enthusiasts seeking to build superior cooling system upgrades. The company remains headquartered in a 68,000-square-foot facility that houses its corporate offices, engineering studio, and testing labs.

The company designs and manufactures performance cooling products including aluminum radiators, intercoolers, oil catch cans, silicone body mounts, and liquid-chill systems. All research and development is conducted in-house using a ROMER Arm, Faro 3D laser scanner, rapid-prototyping 3D printers, computational fluid dynamics analysis, and Dynapack and Dynojet all-wheel-drive dynamometers for validation.

Mishimoto serves automotive enthusiasts across sport compacts, powersports, trucks, Jeeps, muscle cars, daily drivers, and classic vehicles. Its products are used in autocross, drag racing, off-road, and towing applications, with documented collaborations such as a Ford Racing Parts intercooler for the Maverick.

The brand differentiates itself with a lifetime warranty that includes accident protection, direct-stock fitment for straightforward installation, and a global infrastructure that includes offices in Sparks, Nevada, London, Shanghai, and Sydney. Military and first-responder discounts are also offered.

old_description: Located in Pontotoc Mississippi, we have been in business since 2004.  We provide direct service
about:
Mississippi Metal Manufacturing operates from Pontotoc, Mississippi, where it has been in business since 2004. The company is a subsidiary of Moore's Feed, a local agricultural and retail operation, and was established to supply metal building components to the surrounding region.

The firm manufactures "PBR" and "PLP" roof and wall panels in acrylic-coated Galvalume and a range of painted colors, and rolls cold-formed purlins — including Zee, Cee, open-face channel, eave strut, and angle profiles — on site. It also maintains a warehouse stock of structural steel such as I-beams, channel, flat bar, tubing, pipe, and angle iron, along with metal building accessories like roll-up doors, personnel doors, exhaust fans, louvers, and fiberglass and bubble-wrap insulation. Standard panel and trim orders placed before 10 a.m. are available for same-day pickup, while custom purlin orders typically ship within one to three business days.

Its primary customers are home improvement centers, building supply stores, and other retail outlets across Mississippi, Alabama, and Tennessee. The company also serves local retail buyers through Moore's Feed in Pontotoc, providing access to items not commonly carried as off-the-shelf inventory at most retailers.

Mississippi Metal Manufacturing emphasizes timely service and local convenience, offering direct delivery to retail partners and custom trim fabrication to match specific project requirements. The operation is Energy Star certified, reflecting a stated commitment to energy-efficient building products.

name: Missouri Wind and Solar
old_description: PROUDLY DESIGNING AND MANUFACTURING WIND TURBINES AND SOLAR ENERGY SYSTEMS SINCE 2008.
about:
Missouri Wind and Solar is based in Seymour, Missouri. Founded in 2008 by Jeff, who initially opened a store selling ornamental fountains, the business is now owned by his daughter Crystal and her husband Wes, making it a family-owned operation. The venture into wind and solar began when customers noticed the wind turbine powering the warehouse; Jeff, a lifelong tinkerer, disassembled and improved that turbine, sparking the company's focus on renewable energy systems.

The company designs and manufactures its own line of wind turbines and solar energy systems, offering 23 proprietary products alongside components from brands such as Canadian Solar, IronRidge, MidNite Solar, and Victron Energy. Their product range includes wind turbines, solar panels, charge controllers, batteries, inverters, and wiring. They operate with a dedicated team of 13 experts and provide free custom system design services for turnkey wind, solar, or hybrid solutions.

Missouri Wind and Solar serves DIY homeowners, off-grid enthusiasts, educational institutions, and non-profit organizations. A notable example includes a collaborative project between a high school and a non-profit focused on wind energy physics and engineering. They also support RV owners and remote power needs, as evidenced by customer reviews mentioning RV solar system repairs.

The company emphasizes US-sourced products, educational outreach, and empowering customers with hands-on knowledge. Their mission is to help customers achieve energy independence through experienced technical assistance and top-of-the-line products, by example by using their own products in their operations.

Mitchell Plastics operates from Huntsville, Alabama. The business traces its roots to Ultra Manufacturing Ltd., which began in Waterloo, Ontario producing injection-moulded components. No founding year or original founders are disclosed in public records.

The company designs, engineers, and manufactures precision components for automotive interiors. Its capabilities span full-service design, hydrographics, applique, in-mould coating, prototype and production moulds, in-mould assembly tools, and automated robotic assembly. An on-site Innovation Centre demonstrates hydrographics and applique techniques. Facility size, headcount, and annual volumes are not published.

Mitchell Plastics serves the automotive interior sector, supplying components to vehicle manufacturers and tier suppliers. Concrete customer names are not disclosed.

The firm emphasizes a sustainability mindset, reporting that since 2012 multiple solar arrays have generated roughly 730,000 kWh per year, and in 2018 two lithium-ion battery banks were installed to reduce peak power draw. The company also highlights a balance of creativity and engineering through its "Innovation Inside" philosophy.

name: Mitokine Bio Science
old_description: Mitokine Bioscience was founded to impact diabetes care by developing a promising new treatment. That research is now being extended by Diamyd Medical in Sweden. Since opening in 2006, our company has maintained a commitment to innovative research that impacts medical problems and improves the daily lives of patients. Our current focus is providing information on the science of GABA and Alzheimer's disease.
about:
Mitokine Bio Science was founded in 2006 in Hancock, Maine, by Dr. Brooke Ligon, a board-certified neurologist with a doctorate in neuroscience from Tufts Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences. The company began with a mission to develop a novel treatment for diabetes, a research program that has since been taken forward by Diamyd Medical in Sweden.

Today the firm operates as a scientific information resource, concentrating on the biology of GABA and its relevance to Alzheimer’s disease. Dr. Ligon authors and curates the content, drawing on her clinical and research background. No manufacturing facility, production volumes, or part numbers are disclosed; the output is published research summaries and educational material rather than physical goods.

The organization’s work is linked to several academic and philanthropic institutions, including Tufts Medical Center’s Department of Surgery, Molecular Cardiology Research Institute, and GRASP Center, as well as Tufts University’s Neuroscience Department and Vice Provost Office for Industry Collaboration. The Kyle Family Foundation, a charitable entity that supports medical research, is also noted as a connected party. These relationships suggest an audience of researchers, clinicians, and research-funding organizations.

Mitokine states that its distinguishing feature is a sustained commitment to innovative research that addresses medical problems and improves patients’ daily lives. The transition from an internal diabetes drug program to an open information platform on GABA and neurodegeneration reflects that stated purpose.
